query: Current NWS forecast for Death Valley Furnace Creek daily high temperatures July 11-23 2026, and any heat ridge/heat dome building in second half of July 2026 for Death Valley California
answer:
Research complete. Summary of findings for Death Valley (Furnace Creek), July 11-23, 2026:

**NWS Forecast (daily highs):** 113–120°F range across the window. The official NWS forecast (Las Vegas office, as of Jul 14) shows 115°F today, ~119°F Jul 15-16, peaking at **120°F Thursday**, then 116°F Friday, 115°F Saturday. Extended modeling shows highs staying 113-118°F through Jul 23, with a brief monsoon-related dip to ~107°F on July 18. This is **near-to-slightly-above the July normal (~116-117°F) — not record-threatening** (world record is 134°F; recent extreme events ~130°F).

**Heat ridge/dome:** Yes, a significant heat dome is active over the western/central US in mid-to-late July 2026. However, its **core is anchored well east/northeast of Death Valley** (Mountain West/Central US, Denver–Santa Fe–southern Plains corridor), delivering record-threatening heat to the Interior West and Northern Plains rather than to California/the immediate Desert Southwest. Per WeatherWest (Daniel Swain), the ridge stays broad/strong into late July and then shifts westward toward the **Four Corners into a "monsoon high"**, increasing Southwest monsoon moisture — which sustains above-average heat while capping the most extreme readings. The model shows renewed warming to 117-121°F around July 25-27 as that Four Corners ridge re-strengthens.

**Bottom line:** Solidly hot (mid-teens to 120°F) but not historically extreme for Death Valley during this window; Death Valley sits on the warm western flank of the heat dome, not its core.
